_comment: Reviewed Semgrep exceptions for scripts/sast-gate.py. Every finding the p/default ruleset reports must either be fixed or appear here with a disposition ('false-positive' or 'accepted-risk') and a reason a reviewer can check against the code. The gate fails when a finding has no entry, and also when an entry matches nothing (so a fixed finding gets its entry deleted instead of lingering). ERROR-severity findings cannot be excepted. 'match' is the stripped source line at the finding's location: editing that line invalidates the entry on purpose, because the exception was a review of that code.

exceptions.match: log.warning("Could not read BIOS password backup: %s", e)
exceptions.reason: Only substitution is the caught exception. The backup file's contents are never formatted into the message, and the exceptions that can occur here (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError, JSONDecodeError) carry a path or a byte position, not the payload. The rule keys on the word 'password' in the format string.

exceptions.match: with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:  # noqa: S310
exceptions.reason: The URL is a literal https:// constant in this module (the Worker health probe); the variable form is only the Request object built from it. urllib's file:// exposure needs a caller-controlled URL and there is none on this path.

exceptions.match: log.info("BIOS password backup written to %s", BIOS_PASSWORD_BACKUP_FILE)
exceptions.reason: Substitution is the backup file PATH, not the credential. Knowing where the DPAPI-encrypted blob lives does not disclose the BIOS password, and the path is a module constant the operator can already read from the install tree.

exceptions.match: log.error("CRITICAL: Could not write BIOS password backup: %s", e)
exceptions.reason: Substitution is the caught OSError from the atomic write. No part of the encoded credential is formatted into the message.

exceptions.match: log.error("Could not read BIOS password backup: %s", e)
exceptions.reason: Substitution is the caught exception from reading/decoding the backup. A JSONDecodeError reports a line and column, and UnicodeDecodeError reports a byte offset — neither includes the decrypted document.

exceptions.match: log.warning("Could not delete BIOS password backup: %s", e)
exceptions.reason: Substitution is the caught OSError from unlinking the backup file. No credential material is in scope at this line.
Substitution is SET_BIOS_RETURN_CODES.get(rc) — a constant table of firmware return-code NAMES. The password being set is an argument to _set_setting(), not to the logger.
Substitution is SET_BIOS_RETURN_CODES.get(rc), a constant-name lookup. Neither the BIOS password nor the Power-On password reaches the logger.
Substitution is SET_BIOS_RETURN_CODES.get(rc) for the Power-On Password clear failure. The message names the operation, not the credential.
Substitution is SET_BIOS_RETURN_CODES.get(rc) for the Setup password clear failure. The message names the operation, not the credential.

exceptions.match: with urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:  # noqa: S310
exceptions.reason: URL is built from the operator-configured server_url the agent is enrolled with, and the request carries POST data — urllib refuses file:// for a request with a body (ValueError), so the file-read exposure the rule describes is unreachable.

Logs the server's HTTP error body when an uninstall-token request fails, so a failed uninstall is diagnosable. The assumption that this cannot leak the token is now enforced rather than asserted: server/tests/uninstallAuth.test.js drives every error path of both uninstall-auth routes and requires that no response body contains the presented key or token (S252). The token is only returned on a 200.
Substitution is the caught transport exception (URLError/OSError/JSON error). No token material is in the message.

exceptions.match: with urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:  # noqa: S310
exceptions.reason: Same call as the uninstall-token request above: operator-configured server_url, POST body, so file:// is refused by urllib before any read happens.

exceptions.match: os.chmod(str(target), 0o755)  # noqa: S103 -- 0o755 is the correct permission for an executable binary
exceptions.reason: chmod 0o755 is applied to the agent EXECUTABLE after an in-place update — 755 is what makes the new binary runnable. It is not a secret-bearing file; the credential material lives in the DPAPI-protected config, which has its own permissions.

exceptions.match: <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 24 24' fill='%232563eb'%3E%3Cpath d='M12 1L3 5v6c0 5.55 3.84 10.74 9 12 5.16-1.26 9-6.45 9-12V5l-9-4z'/%3E%3C/svg%3E" />
exceptions.reason: The flagged tag is the favicon and its href is a data: URI embedded in the document itself. There is no cross-origin fetch, so there is nothing for an integrity hash to pin.
Joins a CONSTANT filename (CONFIG_FILENAME) onto Electron's app.getPath('userData'). The parameter is supplied by Electron, not by a request, and no request data reaches this function.

Loopback static file server for the built dashboard bundle. It serves files and nothing else — there is no session, cookie or mutating route, so there is no ambient credential a cross-site request could ride.

Express app with no cookie or session authentication: every mutating route authenticates with an Authorization bearer token or API key, which a cross-site form cannot set. CSRF forgery needs ambient credentials, and there are none to forge with.

This proxy exists to terminate TLS for firmware that requires https:// and forward to the plain-HTTP lab server, so the upstream hop is deliberately plaintext and on the local QEMU host bridge. Debug tooling, not shipped.

exceptions.match: with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=15) as response:  # noqa: S310
exceptions.reason: Same proxy on the Python side: the upstream URL is the operator's --upstream argument, defaulting to the QEMU host bridge. The scheme is checked before the request is made (see the S310 comment above it); this tool only runs against the local lab.

The only request-derived value in the chain is a two-value whitelist.

localBinaryPath() has exactly one caller and it passes the literal 'lockdown-installer.exe'. The rule flags the parameter; no request value reaches this join.

The body is a generated PowerShell bootstrap. It cannot be JSON-wrapped (the device writes the response text to disk and runs it) and it is served as text/plain with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff added in S251, so a browser cannot render it as HTML. The hostname interpolated into it has already been through the escapePs1/generateInstallPs1 quoting.
